newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nikkei ends lower, bogged down by gloomy outlook.
newsitem.headline: Nikkei ends lower, bogged down by gloomy outlook.

text.p: Tokyo stocks ended Tuesday trading in negative territory, unable to recover from Monday's losses of more than three percent. Brokers said the market was still disenchanted with the outlook for the economy and the government's economic plans.
The Nikkei 225 finished down 122.18 points, or 0.70 percent, at 17,358.16. Its March futures were down 130 points at 17,330.
"Whenever the Nikkei average hits a floor, it rebounds sharply, but it has failed to do so, meaning there's still more room to fall." a strategist at a second-tier brokerage said.

"There are doubts over the the prime minister's ability to carry out promised reforms, too," he said. "Until the government show signs of doing something favourable for the market, not many investors will feel confident about buying."

At a morning news conference, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka was asked if the ministry saw a need to come up with measures to deal with falling stock prices other than early passage of a supplementary budget for the current fiscal year.
He repeated that stock moves were being watched carefully and that the ministry would make utmost efforts in the management of macroeconomic policies.

The Nikkei has shed more than 20 percent of its worth in recent weeks due to worries about the impact of a scheduled rise in Japan's consumption tax from three to five percent from April 1 and an end to special income tax cuts.
Such worries have been aggravated by a weakening of the yen against the dollar, as this reduces the value of yen-denominated assets, brokers said.
The yen stood at 117.78/88 to the dollar in afternoon Tokyo after falling briefly to the 118 level.
"Its a vicious circle," one strategist said. "The yen weakens on the decaying Nikkei which fuels a stock sell-off."

In other indices, the broader TOPIX was down 9.85 points, or 0.72 percent, at 1,349.32. The Nikkei 300 fell 1.71 points, or 0.66 percent, to 255.47. The second section index fell 10.59 points, or 0.61 percent, to 1,735.01. Turnover was 5.88 million shares against 7.35 million on Monday.
The over-the-counter index was down 8.32 points, or 0.67 percent, at 1,240.69 in afternoon trade.
Some banks continued soft, with Sumitomo Bank Ltd losing 40 yen to 1,360 yen in a trade of 4.916 million shares. It was the third most heavily traded issue on the Tokyo bourse.
Fuji Bank Ltd, ranking fourth with 4.564 million shares traded, also lost 40 yen to 1,350.
Nissan Motor Co Ltd rose four yen to 688 on media reports of robust group profits.

Kokusai Kogyo Co Ltd fell after Janome Sewing Machine Co Ltd said it had bought about 15 million shares in Kokusai from one of Janome's units. It lost 100 yen to 1,080 yen, the third largest percentage loser.
Sakata Seed Corp fell 180 yen to 2,420 yen, the seventh largest percentage loser, daunted by a fall in half-year profits announced on Monday.
On a sector basis, communications, shipbuilding, credit/lease, automobiles and fisheries topped the list of gainers. Oil, foods, air transportation, mining and rubber headed the retreaters.
Brokers said that until market sentiment improved, the shares in the battered banking and construction sectors were likely to be the main target for futures-linked sales.
"When arbitrage-linked positions are unwound, bringing cash stocks within sight of the recent low near 17,000, loss-cutting sales could emerge and prompt a plunge," one broker said.
-- Masako Iijima, Tokyo Equities Desk +81-3-3432-9052
